about: The story of CHASING THE WDC, one card at a time. `at` is when a card is shown: intro (the first time CAREER is opened), pre:<event> (before that event's first start), post:<event> (after its first finish). `if` narrows a post card: met / missed (the objective), champ / notchamp (top of the table when it is shown). `who` empty = the marker pen. At most three short lines a card. ASCII only: the fonts have no other glyphs.

lines: ok. so. you want to be world champion.
by twenty.
it is good to have a plan.
current assets: one borrowed formula 4 car,
one white van whose door only opens from the inside,
one dad.
I did a spreadsheet for the budget.
It says we have minus four hundred dollars and a ham sandwich.
I think the sandwich is in the wrong column.
the car is number 78.
it was the only number left on the sticker sheet.
(remember that. it comes back.)
I am Odd. It is a real name. I checked.
I will be your engineer.
I have brought my own chair.
round one. kate mascoi circuit.
twelve cars. eleven of them have done this before.
Hi! You're the new one. I'm Juno. Car seven.
I'll be at the front if you need anything.
You finished. The car is the same shape as this morning.
By our standards this is a triumph.
That was not the top ten.
I have written it down. I write everything down.
It is mostly this sort of thing.
I filmed the whole race.
My thumb is in most of it.
It's a good thumb, though.
Today is a test day. We are testing you.
The car has already passed.
zandvoort. banking. in the dunes.
dad drove the van onto the beach by mistake.
we do not talk about the beach.
Good race! You're braking too early for turn three, though.
Sorry. Is that annoying? My dad says I'm annoying.
she is right about turn three.
that is the annoying part.
Home race. Half the street came.
Mrs. Albright brought a folding chair and an air horn.
Please don't crash in front of Mrs. Albright.
I measured the crowd. Eleven people.
Mrs. Albright accounted for six of them.
We start last today. There was a paperwork issue.
The issue is that your father did the paperwork.
In my defence, the form had two sides.
suzuka. the track crosses over itself.
nobody told the van's satnav.
the van's satnav has not recovered.
You sat right behind me for a whole lap.
Nobody's done that all year.
...Do it again next time. That was fun.
last round. monza. flat out, brake, pray, repeat.
juno has won this series twice already.
the table is not finished yet.
Season one. Done. We did not run out of money.
We ran out of sandwiches in round two.
But not money.
then a letter came. black envelope. no stamp.
GRAVENMOOR. OCTOBER 31. MIDNIGHT.
BRING THE 78.
Gravenmoor. A village circuit. Closed since 1978.
Car 78 went into the fog on Dead Man's Mile
and did not come out of the other side.
The timing loop still counts one lap, every Halloween.
I do not believe in ghosts.
I do believe in timing loops.
Your grandad was a marshal here. Did I never say?
...Huh.
Thought I'd said.
it came out of the fog with no lights on.
it has your number. literally.
you never saw it brake.
I timed its lap. Then I checked my watch against a second watch.
Both watches are now frightened.
winter. the phone rang.
dad answered it with 'van'.
halloran gt need a second driver.
theirs broke a wrist falling off a podium.
their first driver is juno.
I told them to call you.
Don't make it weird.
I come with the driver. It is in my contract.
I wrote the contract.
Nobody has read it.
They have a truck. With a kitchen in it.
I'm still bringing the van.
For morale.
the off-weekend 'fun race'.
the last car over the line each lap goes home.
nobody here knows what fun is.
Up the hill, flat. Everybody says flat.
Promise me you'll at least think about lifting.
I never do. That's why I'm telling you.
the team 'found' you a newer car.
nobody will say where.
it smells faintly of someone else's air freshener.
Night. Rain. Monaco.
Three things I would not combine.
I have combined them. For science.
the nordschleife. twenty kilometres of it.
one lap. that is the whole race.
nobody has ever finished counting the corners.
team-building day.
somebody booked a demolition derby.
It was me. I have feelings too.
They are mostly this.
last round. you and juno. same car, same team.
next year the team has one seat in formula 1.
one.
they gave the seat to juno.
it had been decided in march. sponsors, and their truck.
it was never about the points.
I found out the same day you did.
I asked them to take both of us. They laughed.
I wasn't joking.
Van's outside when you're ready.
No rush. I parked it badly.
We've got time.
october 31. the black envelope came to the van this time.
it does not care whose truck you arrived in.
Its lap was the same as last year. To the thousandth.
It is not getting slower. You are getting faster.
I resent how pleased I am.
february. no seat.
dad made a new spreadsheet. it had one cell.
the cell said 'hmm'.
Pemberton Grand Prix have finished last in the world. Twice.
They cannot afford a good driver. They can afford you.
I have already said yes for both of us.
formula 1. the big one. hands at ten and two.
your garage is the one next to the bins.
They gave me a team shirt. And a lanyard.
I'm never taking off the lanyard.
Media day. They want us to race each other for the cameras.
Three laps. Same car. Loser buys chips.
I like the big chips.
juno bought the chips.
she got the big ones anyway.
she ate most of yours.
you bought the chips.
the big chips are eleven euros.
dad has opened a new column in the spreadsheet.
summer break.
odd's idea of a holiday is a gravel car park in the mountains.
he has brought his chair.
If it comes down to the last race: no favours. Promise.
I'd never forgive you if you let me win.
Qualifying practice. One lap.
Do not think. Thinking is my job.
You have seen how that goes.
the last round. kate mascoi circuit 2. seven laps.
it comes down to this. it was always going to.
this time it really is about the points.
Whatever happens.
Minus four hundred dollars and a ham sandwich. Look where we are.
Go on. Lights out.
world champion.
you. number 78. the kid from the van.
odd has written it down. he underlined it. twice.
Second in the world. To you, of all people.
...Good.
Now I've got something to chase.
not this year.
dad had the banner printed early. it says CHAMPION.
he is putting it up anyway. 'for next season.'
That was the best race of my life.
Same again next year?
No favours.
one more envelope.
nothing inside this time. only the date.
Your grandad waved the last flag that car ever saw.
He always said somebody should go and finish that race with it.
So. Go on.
it waited on the line until you had crossed. then it left.
it will be there next halloween.
it is very patient.
you led it over the line.
the first time in forty-eight years that it crossed at all.
it pulled alongside. it lifted one hand.
then the fog.
then only the fog.
The loop counted one lap. Then it stopped counting.
I am not crying. It is condensation.
From the fog.
It wasn't the only number left on the sheet, you know.
I just liked how it looked on you.
the end.
(it is never the end. one more race.)
racing for all.
